summary: Compass is a local-first Rust CLI that parses a repository into a queryable dependency graph (via tree-sitter) and delivers the relevant slice two ways: pre-injected into an AI assistant's prompt (plus an MCP server for on-demand queries) and as a live force-directed map in the browser. No network, no API keys, one binary.

sections.body: Layered crates with a language-agnostic core (ADR-0002/0003): compass-core (graph model + query port), compass-extract (stable Extractor trait + tree-sitter harness + registry), compass-engine (walk/index/cache), compass-mcp (MCP tools), compass-viz (visual map), compass-cli (composition root that cfg-gates which languages compile in). A language lives entirely in one compass-lang-<name> crate and never touches core, MCP, or another language.

10 languages shipped: Go, Python, Java, C#, TypeScript (incl. JS/JSX), Rust, Kotlin, Ruby, PHP, C. Adding one = copy compass-lang-template, implement the Extractor trait (detection, grammar, extract, resolve), add the crate to the workspace + an optional dep and lang-<name> feature in compass-cli/Cargo.toml + one register(...) line in registry.rs. Definition of Done in CONTRIBUTING.md §4.

Expand language coverage. C++ is the recommended next add: high real-world usage, mature tree-sitter-cpp grammar, and the existing C crate's quoted-#include resolver is a near-direct reuse. Swift and Scala are the strongest runners-up.
